subject: grayWolf
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: gray wolf standing alert.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
Given the low effort budget, I'm planning a compact but solid wolf model: realistic proportions with a shoulder height around 0.8m and body-plus-tail length near 1.4m, but styled with Warcraft-like exaggeration -- bulky shoulders, a bold mane, battle scars, and maybe glowing eyes or tribal markings.

I'm laying out the skeleton structure -- hips as the root joint, a spine chain built from catmull curve points running from hips to chest, then a neck chain into head and jaw joints, plus a tail chain extending back from the hips, all tied together with limb bones. For the body geometry I'm sweeping a tube along the spine path using a radius function for the torso shape, making sure the spine chain is properly parented to the hips joint so the sweep deforms correctly.

Now I'm adding the neck sweep tapering toward the head, then building head details -- a sphere-based skull, a frustum-shaped snout, a separate jaw joint for the lower jaw, cone ears and teeth, and amber glowing eye planes. For the ruff I'm scattering fur-tuft cards around the neck and shoulders using a surface filter, and starting on the leg limbs for front and back pairs.

I'm positioning the paw spheres so their scaled bottoms sit right at the floor, then checking that the front leg's total length exactly reaches from shoulder height down to the foot target, confirming the straightened pose will sit flush on the ground.

Now I'm working out hind leg reach with a three-segment chain from hip to foot, then placing shoulder and hip joints with their x/z/y offsets and setting proper parent joints for the leg chains. I'm also sketching the tail as a curving chain from the hip area down and back, parented to the hips, using a tapered sweep that goes gray-to-dark at the tip with extra thickness for a bushy look.

For the coat, I'm layering a mottled gray countershade paint with a cream belly tone, keeping legs matching and skipping extra sock gradients for simplicity. Then I'm setting up the head: orienting it forward and slightly downward off the neck joint, building a skull as a scaled sphere, and shaping the snout as a tapering frustum extending forward and slightly down from the head.

Now I'm continuing the snout taper down to a smaller width, placing a dark nose sphere at the tip, and setting up the jaw as a child joint of the head with its own forward-aiming frustum and conical teeth. For the ears, I'm positioning spike-shaped cones off the top of the head, working out how to mirror the left/right placement using a sign multiplier on the local coordinates.

Setting up the head joint parented to the neck's end, then laying out the neck path and head center position. I'm placing the skull sphere, snout box, and glowing amber eye planes relative to the head center with specific offsets for a wolf-like proportioned head.

Checking the eye placement against the skull ellipsoid surface math shows the eyes would hover slightly outside the skull, so instead I'm switching to decal onto the skull mesh for a cleaner fit.

I'm also planning brow ridges as small wedge details or folded into the eye texture itself, and I'm sketching out a ruff/mane made of scattered pointed tuft card textures around the neck and shoulders for a spiky, layered look.

For Warcraft-style flair, I'm adding oversized spiked shoulder fur, a bone-fang necklace or leather strap with war paint, glowing eyes, and a scar. I'm working out how to wrap a strap or loop ring around the neck using the skeleton's joint position so it cuts cleanly around the neck without accidentally slicing through the body.

Now I'm hanging bone fangs along that neck loop as downward-pointing spikes, and setting up the glowing eyes using a glow effect imported from the kit's glow module, keeping color usage within limits before writing the final code.

I'm defining the body radius function with chest depth tapering along the spine, setting up the spine chain with three joints rooted at the hips, and routing a tail chain back and down from the hip area with a darker tip color banding toward the end.

For the head, I'm placing spike-cone ears on the skull angled upward and outward with a smaller dark inner cone, and adding fangs as cones—upper ones pointing down from the snout, lower ones pointing up from the jaw, with the jaw shaped as a tapered frustum box.

For feet, I'm using small spheres scaled into toe-like shapes with dark cone claws pointing forward, positioned off the last point of each limb chain.

Now I'm writing the sweep calls to draw the legs along their joint chains using the coat color.

Checking overall proportions - the body stretches from roughly z -0.5 to 1.05, tail extending to -1.15, giving about 2.2 meters total, a bit bigger than a real wolf but fitting the stylized scale I'm going for.

Placing the hip and shoulder joints and double-checking the leg reach distances line up with the segment lengths. Then I'm designing the eye texture with an almond-shaped amber iris, slit pupil, and dark brow stroke, sized to fit as a mirrored decal on both eyes, plus adding the skull geometry as a sphere attached to the head bone.

Now I'm scattering fur tufts across the neck and body surfaces, filtering by position and normal direction so they only appear on the upper back areas, using a grey gradient texture tinted to match the coat color.
